checks: Uniform normalized cap discrepancy yields eventual positive fine mass. At fixed l, only finitely many sampled (z,u) fibers occur. With s>0, moving within one such fiber changes only the thresholds of cuts with nonzero last-coordinate normal; after normalizing that part, a bounded slab estimate is uniform over orientations. Hence the depth is continuous on each compact fine fiber. For s=0 the feasible trace is finite. In both cases the maximum exists.

Along a subsequence realizing the liminf, pass to convergent normalized coarse mass ratios. A positive-weight source in an integer anchored representation contributes a translate of its coefficient-scaled body to the target, so the limiting mass ratio there is at least that positive source ratio times the coefficient to power m. P_+ is lattice-complete, its mass fraction tends to one, and its retained hull has exactly these fibers.

The induced lattice is the full intersection with the affine span, not the potentially smaller subgroup generated by the sites. The accepted saturated lattice chart has rank k′≤k, leaves the original continuous coordinates untouched, and preserves restricted closed-cap masses. The retained raw cap bound yields the factor M_{l,+}/M_l in full coarse normalized depth.

The compact lift has full ambient dimension k′+D and exact intrinsic trace dimension m because every limiting fiber is a positive m-body. Its normalized mass is one. The needed sharp premise is only the actual pair (k′,D), with k′≤k<k+r and m≤D≤B(k′,m)≤B(k,m). The bound B is increasing because B(k+1,m)−B(k,m)=(m+1)2^k−1>0. At rank zero the lift is one ordinary m-body, D=m, so the centroid input suffices.

Starting from a feasible limit mark, within-fiber continuity gives a relative interior mark in that same fiber with depth loss at most epsilon. Support function convergence preserves a smaller residual ball at its fixed coordinates. The summed symmetric-difference masses in the fixed planes tend to zero, controlling every cap at that same mark. Pushforward returns a feasible original coarse point and retaining the other fibers loses only the vanishing mass factor.

If w_l+rho A_l B_2^m lies in R B_2^m, opposite points in each unit direction give 2rho |A_l u|≤2R. Thus the least singular value is at least M_{l,+}/(R/rho)^(m−1), with the product of no other singular values equal to one for m=1. The concentric source radius is exactly bounded below by rho^m M_{l,+}/R^(m−1).

The locally finite union of closed sample cubes is closed and already covers almost every fine base by the tiling, hence covers every base. The original-grid move has norm at most sqrt(r) delta_l, which is o(M_{l,+}) and so feasible. Through-mark cuts with unit coarse continuous normal lose at most kappa_{m−1} R^(m−1) times the movement per fiber; pure coarse-base cuts do not move. Taking the infima of these closed cuts and dividing by M_l gives the exact stated loss.

Transfer cap depth at the same feasible rounded mark using discrepancy. Monotonicity of gamma and k′≤k yield the displayed liminf. Since gamma_B>1/e>1/4 and gamma_s≤1/2 for s≥1 by the binomial expansion, the target is at most 2^(−k)/4 for s≥1 or for s=0,r≥2. The positive strict gap gives the eventual finite guarantee. For s=0,r=1 the limit comparison cannot supply that implication. The common covolume cancels.

This allows a point of the body outside its mixed trace, while the proof needs the supplied point to lie in one sampled fiber. A depth bound alone does not imply that membership.

issues.repair: Replace “has a point of normalized depth” with “has a point in its mixed trace of normalized depth”. This is the intended premise of the original source.
